Built-in ImageGen mode. Existing skitter walking atlas used as identity/style reference.

Initial generation prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production RGBA sprite atlas for a pixel-style hack-and-slash RPG with an orthographic 45-degree elevated camera. Image 1 is a STYLE AND CREATURE IDENTITY REFERENCE ONLY, not an edit target. Preserve this same low armored skitter beetle: blue-grey segmented carapace, cream/bone horn edges and curved mandibles, six dark articulated legs, small amber eyes. Preserve the crunchy pixel edges, restrained texture, warm highlights and neutral shadow colors of the reference. No floor, no cast shadow, no backdrop, no UI, no words, no grid lines, no letters, no borders, no numbers, no particles, no speed streaks. Truly transparent alpha background. Each pose must be completely separated by generous transparent gutters. Keep the body scale and ground contact origin constant across each row. Never translate the whole creature forward between poses; animation happens in place. Only one creature per cell. Keep all legs and horns connected to the body, including death poses. Render a clean rectangular sheet with evenly spaced rows and columns. Draw sprites small, around 55 percent of cell width and 60 percent of cell height, with at least 25 percent total transparent side padding. Five directional rows from top to bottom: South (front toward viewer), Southeast (front-right diagonally), East (profile facing RIGHT), Northeast (rear-right diagonally), North (back away from viewer). All five rows use the same elevated camera, not a top-down overhead sketch. Do not turn the E or SE rows left. Reuse exactly the same anatomy, shell segments and horn arrangement in all poses. Produce exactly FIVE ROWS by SIX COLUMNS, 30 sprites total. Read each row left to right: column 1 HIT REACTION, shell tilted back slightly with forelegs recoiling; column 2 recovered planted stance matching the reference body height; column 3 DEATH START, upright buckling legs and sagging shell; column 4 collapse, legs fold inward and shell drops halfway; column 5 fallen carcass, body resting low with curled legs; column 6 final still carcass, same collapsed silhouette with mandibles and legs fully still. Keep the carcass oriented in the row's original direction, with all limbs still attached and a readable low silhouette. Death is a visible four-step collapse rather than disappearing. No gore. Never make the final carcass tall; keep its original body size and show the height loss through the collapse. The standing/recovered poses establish the same ground line in all columns. No detached debris, no dust, no shadows. Keep every sprite inside its own equally sized cell. Make a broad rectangular atlas with five clearly aligned rows.

Final correction prompt:
Edit target: the supplied five-row six-column skitter hurt/death atlas. Its background already has transparent alpha, but remove any remaining visible soft brown halo and floor/contact shadow outside the 30 creature silhouettes. Preserve the existing transparent background and return genuine RGBA alpha transparency, with no colored matte or checkerboard drawing. Preserve every creature silhouette, internal shadows, pixel colors, horns, legs, proportions, directions, poses, exact row/column arrangement, body scale and placement. Do not resize, move, redesign, rotate or reanimate any sprite. Keep all 30 sprites fully separated as transparent cutouts, with clean dark pixel outlines and intact limb/horn edges. No text, particles, grid lines, background glow or cast shadows. Only clean the cutout edges and external floor shadow.
